newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi rebels battle government troops-aid agency.
newsitem.headline: Burundi rebels battle government troops-aid agency.

text.p: An aid agency evacuated its staff from southern Burundi on Sunday after heavy fighting between Hutu rebels and government troops, aid officials said.

Ahmed Jabri, operations co-ordinator for the International Medical Corps (IMC) told reporters six IMC staff had been evacuated to Bujumbura after two days of heavy fighting around Rutana, 175 km (110 miles) southeast of Bujumbura, on Sunday.
The aid workers said the rebels had attacked a secondary school, but there were no reports of casualties in the attack.
"Their aim appears to be to cut off the south of Burundi," they said. An army spokesman confirmed the rebel attack, but had no details of any casualties.

Last week, Hutu rebels attacked another school in nearby Buta, killing 36 students and seven staff, and a Swiss nun and her Burundian driver were killed when their vehicle hit a landmine 20 km (12 miles) south of Bujumbura.
Hutus make up about 85 percent of Burundi's population, but the minority Tutsis dominate the government and the army.
At least 150,000 civilians have been killed in violence and civil war in the last four years. An army coup last year overthrew the civilian government and installed Pierre Buyoya as president.
